youtubeTitle: The Gospel and Soul Health Session 24 - Dr Bruce Wauchope
topic: Test of faith and the inner rod of iron
summary: Bruce defines faith as receiving a spoken relationship on the inside, as Abram did, not as standing on Bible verses until we believe them. The 'test of faith' in 2 Corinthians 13:5 is whether we know Jesus Christ is in us. He honours the Bible as 'the word of the Word', but notes that Moses sprinkled even the book with blood: Scripture serves to unveil Christ and is not itself the relationship. He leads a prayer asking the Spirit to open our eyes to Christ within and to expose and release 'agreements with darkness'. He then explains Christ's rule 'with a rod of iron' (Psalm 2; Psalm 110) as working inside-out and bottom-up: relentlessly but never violating our will, it breaks the 'broken cisterns' of religion and self-protection so that we can receive love.
keyPoints: At Babel the nations were handed over to the 'sons of God' (Deuteronomy 32:8, Septuagint). God then began relating through Abram to win them all back.
Faith is receiving a spoken relationship on the inside: Abram believed God. It is not memorising verses and 'standing on them' until you believe.
'Faith comes by hearing the word of Christ': God and Christ are in you, so you listen on the inside.
The test of faith (2 Corinthians 13:5) is 'Do you not know that Jesus Christ is in you?', not 'Have you got your stuff together?'

The Bible is precious, 'the word of the Word', but Jesus alone is the Word. Moses sprinkled even the book with blood (Hebrews 9:19), so its purpose is to unveil Christ rather than to replace relationship with Him.
Faith as inner dialogue: Christ says 'You're mine; I loved you before creation; let me love you; abide with me in your pain', and we respond, even with 'I'll try, it's hard.'
If you can't hear Christ within, He is still there. Ask the Spirit to expose and remove the 'agreements with darkness' that leave you deaf and blind, then renounce them.

Prayer themes: open my eyes to Christ in me; change my worldview, thoughts and emotions; let me share Christ's heart and the Father's love, including in my dark bits; conform my body to Christ; let me see Christ in others. 'Thank you, more please.'
Christ in us is relentless in love but never violates or breaks our will. He addresses again and again whatever reduces our flow of life and love.

The 'rod of iron' (Psalm 2) works inside-out and bottom-up, not as top-down smashing or a theocracy. It breaks the 'broken cisterns' (Jeremiah 2:13) of religion, climbing to God and conscience-based living.
Like a parent gently removing something harmful from a child, Christ cracks structures that stop us knowing we are loved, so we can 'embrace it, more please.'
'Kiss the Son' means relating back on the inside: hug back, respond in your belly and heart. Each person works with Father and Son in their own unique way; there is no cookie cutter.

keyTerms.definition: Receiving and responding to a spoken relationship with Christ on the inside, not mental assent to texts.
Whether you know that Jesus Christ is in you (2 Corinthians 13:5).
Scripture as the written witness that unveils Jesus, who alone is 'the Word'.
Inner collusions, beliefs and patterns that keep us blind and deaf to Christ's presence and love.
Christ's relentless, loving rule from inside us, breaking structures that block life and love.
Self-made religious and defensive structures that cannot hold the living water (Jeremiah 2:13).
God's way of transforming from within humanity's flesh upward, rather than imposing from above.
Responding back to Christ within in relationship: hugging back and relating.

quotes: Faith is receiving a spoken relationship on the inside.
This is not 'the Word'. This has the word of 'the Word' in it.
He never violates us, never breaks our will, but He's pretty relentless in how He loves us.
It's not top down, it's bottom up.

caseStudy.title: Verses on the fridge
caseStudy.scenario: Priya, 41, covers her fridge with promise verses and recites them each morning, trying to 'believe hard enough' that her chronic worry will lift. When the worry persists she concludes her faith is weak and feels ashamed. She has never thought of faith as listening to Someone within her. Lately she has also noticed that she keeps a tight 'everything is fine' front at church.
caseStudy.analysis: Priya is treating faith as standing on texts, effort aimed at the Book, rather than a spoken relationship with Christ in her. Her 'everything is fine' front is a broken cistern, a defence that keeps love out. Bruce's teaching suggests the real test is knowing Christ is in her, and that He will gently and persistently work from within on structures that block love, without forcing her.
pathway: Keep loving Scripture, but read it as the 'word of the Word', asking 'Jesus, what are You saying to me through this?'
Ask quietly, 'Jesus Christ, are You in me?', listen, and journal whatever comes.
Pray for the Spirit to show any 'agreements with darkness', such as 'I must look fine to be accepted', and renounce them.
Practise 'kissing the Son': answer His love with simple responses like 'I am Yours.'
Share honestly with one safe friend, and see a GP or counsellor if the worry keeps disrupting daily life.

practices.name: The listening question
practices.how: Sit quietly and ask, 'Jesus Christ, are You in me?' Listen inwardly for a few minutes and write down whatever you sense. If nothing comes, rest in the fact that He is there.

practices.name: Releasing agreements
practices.how: Ask the Holy Spirit to show where you agree or collude with darkness (fear, shame, self-protection). List them and quietly renounce each: 'I don't agree with this; please remove it.'

practices.name: Thank you, more please
practices.how: When you notice Christ's love breaking through, or a defence cracking, respond with 'Thank you, more please,' welcoming His inner work rather than resisting it.

reflection: Is my faith mainly something I do with texts, or a relationship I listen to and answer on the inside?
What 'broken cisterns' have I built that Christ may be gently cracking right now?
How do I react to the idea that Christ is relentless in love but never forces my will?

quiz.q: According to Bruce, what is the 'test of faith' in 2 Corinthians 13:5?
options: Whether you have memorised key verses
Whether you know that Jesus Christ is in you
quiz.explain: Paul says to examine yourself: 'Do you not know that Jesus Christ is in you?'

quiz.q: Why does Bruce mention Moses sprinkling the book with blood?
options: To show that the Bible is worthless
To show that Scripture serves to unveil Christ, the true Word, and is not the relationship itself
To prove that the Torah was written by Moses alone
quiz.explain: The book was 'good enough for its purpose': revealing Jesus, who alone is the Word.

quiz.q: How does Christ's 'rod of iron' operate in this teaching?
options: Inside-out and bottom-up, relentlessly but never violating our will
Only at the end of history
quiz.explain: Christ breaks unworkable structures from within as a loving parent would, without forcing the will.
